## Intent
Hypothesis: branchless blend of the death verdict eliminates branch misprediction in the respawn path, allowing the vectorized position update to stream close to the memory floor.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout packs 68 B/particle; loop 1 touches 32 of 68 bytes (47% hot — age+pos+seed+vel) and loop 2 touches 28 (41% hot — color+pos), so over half each cache line drags is dead weight. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers. The working set spills L1d at N≈481, L2 at N≈7710, L3 at N≈246723; with only 47% hot bytes, effective streaming demand is modest, but the blend approach trades branch elimination for instruction count, making instruction delivery — not data residency — the binding constraint.

## Cache saturation
Cost is flat across regimes: 20.3 ns/p at N=320 (L1d) rises to ~25 ns/p at N=10M (DRAM) at q=0.01 — a 25% increase where a bandwidth-bound algo would see 2-3x. No sharp knee at any spill: L1d→L2 adds ~0.2 ns/p, L2→L3 adds ~0.5, L3→DRAM adds ~1. At q=0.5, cost is essentially flat at 31-32 ns/p across all N, confirming the bottleneck is instruction delivery, not data movement.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.1-3.4 GB/s — 17-27% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — against a memory floor of 5.359 ns/p that the algo exceeds by 3.7-6x. This is frontend-bound: 70% frontend stalls, 0% branch flush everywhere. Against naive scalar the blend is marginally faster (0.91-0.98x); against the winner (AF02.LP1-autovec.LP2-opt) it is 1.7-3.4x slower. The gap narrows with death rate — 2.74x winner at q=0.01 N=320 versus 1.91x at q=0.5 — because the scalar respawn path penalizes both algos at high q.

## Assembly
Loop 1 partially vectorizes position: `vmovups` loads 16 B, `vmulps`/`vaddps` update xyz, `vshufps`/`vinsertps` reshuffle, `vmovlps` stores back. But the death check is still branchy (`vucomiss`+`jbe`), and respawn is entirely scalar — `imul`/`shr`/`xor` for hash RNG, `movzx` for extraction, 13 byte-granular stores. Loop 2 is fully scalar: `vucomiss` for clamping, `movzx`/`cmovae` for saturation, 16 byte-granular `mov BYTE PTR` stores. Only 26 of 383 instructions (7%) are vectorized; 320 instructions/particle explain the 70% frontend stall — decode cannot feed execution.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.91-0.98x of naive baseline and 1.7-3.4x slower than the winner at every point. The blend eliminates branches that were never costly (branch_flush=0%) but generates 320 instructions/particle that stall the frontend at 70%. Partial vectorization (`vmulps` on position) cannot offset the scalar respawn and byte-granular scatter, capping bandwidth at 17-27% of ceiling.
